[C112 · daily · Jordan Velez] If the small places are the reason Uptown feels like a neighborhood, it is fair to ask who benefits when the neighborhood gets more valuable. The answer is not settled by asking. My mother ran a laundromat on 7th Street, and her customers kept coming right up until the building sold. Regulars are loyal. Loyalty does not pay a landlord who has watched the office tenants next door. Nakamura's regulars are still coming in. Lopez's machine is still running. The block is moving.
